headlines.title: Skydance outlines its $6 billion in planned cost savings. Here's the breakdown
headlines.summary: The updates came alongside a third-quarter earnings report for the legacy Paramount Skydance.
headlines.article_text: Skydance $6 billion cost savings breakdown Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Skydance has said it plans to cut $6 billion in costs over the next three years. On Monday, it outlined where those savings would come from, including marketing spend and the consolidation of streaming and broadcast operations. The updates came alongside a third-quarter earnings report for the legacy Paramount Skydance. In this article SKYD Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT David Ellison, co-chief executive officer of Skydance Corp., left, and Ynon Kreiz, co-chief executive officer of Skydance Corp., right, at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Skydance is pulling back the curtain on how it plans to achieve at least $6 billion in cost savings in the next three years. "By combining two global streaming services, two film and TV studio groups, two television portfolios, and overlapping corporate functions, we can reduce duplicative spend across an expense base of more than $50 billion," the company wrote in a letter to shareholders Monday as part of Paramount Skydance's third-quarter earnings release. Skydance, the newly formed combination of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery, said it projects at least $2.2 billion in cost reductions from eliminating "redundant back-office and corporate functions," including eliminating management layers and ramping the use of artificial intelligence. Those savings also account for "rationalizing" its office footprint. Skydance expects at least $1 billion in savings from streamlining marketing and promotional spending. And around $1.4 billion in savings will come from unifying its streaming businesses and broadcast architecture and integrating back-end technology. A final $1.4 billion in savings will be tied to "optimizing third-party spend," eliminating overlapping expenses, and consolidating purchasing decisions to one centralized group, Skydance said. "We are confident in achieving these savings, drawing on our playbook from Paramount," the company wrote. "That program is on track to achieve over $2.7 billion in run-rate efficiencies by the end of 2026." Some of that cost-cutting has already begun. Last month, Skydance began offering voluntary buyouts to employees ahead of official layoffs. At the same time, the company adopted a five-day-per-week in-office policy. Additionally, last week saw the departure of eight executives — four from Warner Bros. and four from Paramount. The company has previously said it plans to eventually merge the Paramount+ and HBO Max streaming services into a single platform. On Monday, Skydance said it would take the first step toward that goal early next year, offering a bundle of the streaming services "at an even greater value." Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz told investors during the company's earnings call that Skydance is also looking for ways to optimize its content budget. The company spends more than $30 billion annually on shows and films. "As one company, we can make smarter choices about how we distribute and monetize both new content and library content," Kreiz said. Skydance noted that it's expecting a $200 million headwind in the fourth quarter from theatrical underperformances at Warner Bros. studio related to already launched titles and upcoming releases. The company will also utilize AI to speed up production and decrease costs to make films, co-CEO and chairman David Ellison said on the call. "We think these tools will help unlock more original storytelling by being able to make the budget more digestible to be able to take that amount of risk," Ellison said. The updates came alongside third-quarter results for the legacy Paramount Skydance company that included revenue of $7.03 billion, which was roughly in line with StreetAccount estimates of $7.04 billion, and adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $1 billion, topping StreetAccount estimates of $913.5 million. However, adjusted earnings per share of 45 cents were not immediately comparable to StreetAccount EPS estimates. The results don't include the impact of the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, which closed after the end of the third quarter. Skydance detailed business units of the combined entity including studios, direct-to-consumer and TV, and said it will provide full-year guidance during its fourth-quarter earnings report early next year. "Going forward, we will provide guidance on an annual basis, as we prioritize long-term value creation, which we believe will be more consistent with our strategic approach," the company told shareholders. "We will continue to provide quarterly updates, including certain forward-looking commentary where applicable, which will give investors visibility into our near-term progress of the business." headlines.article_text: Stock market movers: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, speaking on CNBC's Squawk Box on Sept. 28th, 2026. CNBC Traders closely watched quarterly results rolling in from entertainment giant Skydance and electronic manufacturing firm Sanmina after the market close. Both names diverged sharply, with Skydance skidding on a newly announced plan to cut $6 billion in costs. Sanmina, however, jumped on a rosy outlook. The stock market wrapped up Monday's trading on a strong note, with the S&P 500 rising more than 2% for its best session since April. The action comes after a losing week that was largely led by declines in tech. The sector saw a rebound to begin this week, but Nvidia sat out Monday's rally after CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Follow below as CNBC breaks down the biggest stock market moves of the day: 54 Min Ago Trade Desk shares surge following better-than-expected earnings, strong outlook Shares for the Trade Desk jumped over 19% after the company reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. The global advertising technology company earned 33 cents a share on an adjusted basis and notched revenue of $736 million. That's higher than the 25 cents per share and $650 million anticipated by analysts polled by LSEG. Trade Desk in the past day The company also sees fourth-quarter revenue of at least $755 million, trouncing the $650 million estimate. Guidance for adjusted EBITDA in the current quarter also came in sharply above estimates. — Ananya Chetia 1 Hour Ago Sanmina surges in extended trading as guidance tops estimates Shares of electronic manufacturing services provider Sanmina soared after the company rolled out an outlook that came in ahead of the Street's expectations. The stock was last up 20% in extended trading. Sanmina in the past day Sanmina sees full-year earnings in a range of $15.50 to $17.50 per share, topping the FactSet consensus estimate of $14.07 a share. The company's revenue forecast of $17.5 billion to $19.5 billion also came in ahead of the $16.61 billion consensus estimate. — Darla Mercado 1 Hour Ago Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition. Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year. Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed. Read the full story and watch our exclusive interview with Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo here . — Tanaya Macheel 1 Hour Ago Skydance shares fall after entertainment giant announces cost-cutting plans Skydance , the combined entity of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, said that it plans to cut $6 billion in costs over the next three years. Shares of Skydance were last down roughly 2%. The company said that the cost savings would come from marketing spend and the consolidation of its streaming and broadcast operations. Further, the legacy Paramount Skydance, the predecessor company of Skydance, reported third-quarter revenue that fell short of expectations. Revenue in the period came in at $7.03 billion, while analysts polled by StreetAccount sought $7.04 billion. Read more from CNBC's Sarah Whitten about Skydance's cost-cutting plans . — Darla Mercado 1 Hour Ago Rocket Lab slumps after third-quarter loss comes in wider than anticipated The manufacturer of spacecraft slid about 3% in extended trading after Rocket Lab reported a loss in the third quarter. Rocket Lab in the past day The company posted a loss of 12 cents per share, missing the FactSet consensus estimate for a loss of 7 cents a share. Revenue, however, surpassed estimates, landing at $267.8 million versus the Street's expectation of $257.2 million. Rocket Lab also said it anticipates negative adjusted EBITDA in a range of $14 million to $20 million, worse than the FactSet consensus estimate for negative EBITDA of $10.9 million. —Darla Mercado 1 Hour Ago Plug Power jumps 4% following earnings report Plug Power shares rose after the company's third-quarter results topped estimates. The company reaffirmed its full-year guidance, with revenue growth expected to range from 15% to 16% year over year. Shares were last up 4%. Plug Power in the past day — Ananya Chetia 2 Hours Ago Lucid Group falls on wider-than-expected loss in third quarter Shares for electric vehicle manufacturer Lucid Group shed over 3% after the company missed on revenue against analysts polled by LSEG. The company reported $350.3 million in revenue versus the LSEG consensus call for $407 million. Lucid also reported a wider-than-expected loss of $2.74 per share, while analysts sought a loss of $2.28 a share. — Ananya Chetia 5 Hours Ago First Solar slumps on price target cut from Piper Sandler Solar panels made by First Solar are seen at the Overland Park Solar Array in Toledo, Ohio, Oct. 5, 2021. The firm trimmed its price target on First Solar to $222 from $251, calling for nearly 10% upside from Friday's close. Piper Sandler trimmed its full-year 2026 revenue estimate by 2.6%, and noted that it's paying close attention to what happens to First Solar's volumes after 2028, particularly as the company shifts away from its current long-term contract structure.
